objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with vulvar itching and discomfort.

fragments.text: The patient presents with a year-long history of severe vulvar itching and pain during sexual intercourse that has gradually worsened. She has tried over-the-counter lubricants without significant relief. Menopause occurred 8 years ago. Her medical history is significant for diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diet-controlled), hypertension (treated with hydrochlorothiazide), menopause at 52 years of age.
Married, sexually active with her husband until recently due to severe pain. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially.
Denies urinary incontinence, postcoital bleeding, or recent changes in skin elsewhere on the body.

exam_leaves.text: Dry, thin, white plaque-like lesions on the vulva. Atrophy of the labia minora and retraction of the clitoris. Pale and wrinkled perianal skin.
No vaginal discharge or bleeding. Vaginal mucosa appears atrophic.
Nontender uterus and adnexa. No masses palpated.

test_leaves.text: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
Hyperkeratosis with a thinning of the epidermis and loss of rete ridges, sclerotic changes in the dermis.
6.5 mmol/L (117 mg/dL) - Indicative of controlled diabetes.
